name: AllInOneTools Site Audit
author: Bhavin Sheth

sections.description:
Site Audit checks your whole website and writes a report that says what was found and how to fix it, in plain words.

What it checks

  • Technical SEO: robots.txt, sitemap, noindex, canonical, redirects, SSL, broken links, compression, caching.
  • On-page SEO for every page and post: titles, descriptions, headings, image alt text, internal links, schema, readability.
  • AdSense readiness: policy pages, enough content, thin pages, ads.txt, consent banner, navigation. A checklist, not a promise: approval is Google’s decision.
  • Trust (E-E-A-T): author, dates, About and Contact detail, Organization schema.
  • AI search readiness: which AI crawlers robots.txt allows, llms.txt, question headings, FAQ sections, text readable without JavaScript.
  • Speed and mobile, security, e-mail and domain, and WordPress health (orphan pages, uncategorized posts, SEO plugin conflicts).

What you get

  • One overall score, a score per section, and a “Fix these first” list.
  • Audit the whole site or a single page. The audit runs in the background; you can close the page.
  • A score for every page, shown in the report, the Posts list and the editor. “Re-check” scans one page again after you fix it.
  • The plugin screens are ready for translation. The report text is written in English.
  • Print the report or save it as a PDF from your browser.
  • Tools: AI crawler rules for robots.txt, an llms.txt generator, internal link ideas.

What it does not do

  • It does not measure keyword rankings, backlinks, Domain Authority or competitor traffic. That data is not public.
  • It cannot tell how often ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity mention your site. “AI search readiness” checks that your site is ready to be read.
  • It does not guarantee rankings or AdSense approval.

Site Audit Pro

A separate add-on, sold by the author, adds competitor comparison, AI help with your own Google Gemini key, Word and CSV reports with your logo, the report in 7 more languages, domain expiry and spam blacklist checks, client share links, audits of other websites, and automatic audits with e-mail reports. Everything listed above works without it.

External services

The audit runs on your own server. Nothing is sent to the plugin author.

The plugin requests the public pages of your own website to read them (for a single-page audit, the one page address you enter). It also asks your server’s normal DNS resolver for the DNS records of your own domain (SPF, DMARC, MX).

One outside service is used, and only if you choose to add a key for it:

Google PageSpeed Insights API

  • What it is used for: to add Google’s speed scores (performance score, LCP, CLS, INP) to the report.
  • What is sent, and when: the address of the audited page and your own API key are sent to Google when an audit runs. Nothing is sent if you have not saved a PageSpeed key in the API Keys tab.
  • Provided by Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip in Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, and activate it.
  2. Open Site Audit in the admin menu.
  3. Check the policy page links and press Start audit.
  4. Optional: add the free Google PageSpeed key in the API Keys tab.
sections.faq:
How long does an audit take?

It depends on your hosting. One page takes under a minute. A site with 50 posts takes a few minutes. Several hundred posts can take 15 minutes or more.

Can I close the page while it runs?

Yes. The audit runs on your server in small steps. On a site with very few visitors, add a real cron job (see the Help tab) so background work keeps moving.

Do I need an API key?

No. The Google PageSpeed key is optional and free. Without it you get every check except the PageSpeed scores.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

Audits, settings, keys and scores.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Changes asked for in the WordPress.org review: every settings field is cleaned as it is read, all printed HTML goes through wp_kses, and CSS and scripts are added with the enqueue functions.
  • The plugin no longer contacts rdap.org or spam blacklists. The only outside service is Google PageSpeed Insights, and only with your own key.
  • Report language packs are no longer bundled.

1.1.0

  • Pro features moved to a separate add-on. The free plugin keeps the full audit, print/PDF and the tools.

1.0.2

  • Edit links in the report open in a new tab, so the report stays open.

1.0.1

  • Another website: choose how many pages to read (40 to 500); the report says when it is a sample.
  • Pages count as content, not only posts (for sites built from pages).
  • Lazy-loaded images are read correctly.
  • The Audit tab shows clearly which audit is running.

1.0.0

  • First release.
